A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the control of responding is determined by the reinforcement schedule, but the relative amounts of this control are dependent on the difficulty of the task.
the control exerted over behavior by the reinforcement schedule is independent of the intensity control exerted by a stimulus dimension.
the relative control of schedule and intensity is determined by a function that is dependent on the intensity of the sound and the discrimination difficulty.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concurrent assessment of schedule and stimulus control across successive discrimina- tions is an effective method for studying the interaction of these two variables.
the relative control exerted by schedule and intensity is not constant across successive discriminations, but rather varies as a function of the difficulty of the task.
concurrent assessment of schedule and stimulus control is feasible and may be useful.
